request.decision: Does the supplied participant workflow evidence justify starting one next-stage purpose-distinction experiment?

candidates.description: Start one minimal experiment distinguishing further research from readiness to wait for a possible action, keeping unresolved interpretation questions open.
Reuse the existing two-way workflow for one focused clarification without adding features.
Make no prototype change and defer a stage decision pending additional participant evidence.

request.evidence: The completion criterion is a participant research-and-review cycle in each direction, an expressed use or limitation of related information, and traceable original and subsequent records for both objects. Previously only one direction had participant evidence. New feedback supplies the reverse cycle with separate saved judgments and later review, calls the related object another reference dimension, and identifies a dated difference. A change-selection conflicts with terse unchanged-sounding text. A quantity assertion lacks data, and the judgment-quality review is inconclusive. Both outcomes were already familiar; this is not an independent baseline.
request.priorities: Assess process exploration only, not method effectiveness. Do not infer understanding from completed forms. Select one useful next question without requiring conceptual mastery. No automated conclusions or full management system. A model ranking is advisory, not completion evidence.
requirements: Both workflow directions have actual participant research and review evidence.
The participant describes a use or limitation of related information.
Original and later records remain traceable without rewriting.
The next step tests one unresolved purpose distinction and preserves uncertainty.
